```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

anndata.claude is an R port of Python anndata.
Its first priority is that `.h5ad` files round trip between R and Python.

```{r library}
library(anndata.claude)
```

## Create an AnnData

An `AnnData` holds a matrix `X` with observations (`obs`) as rows and variables (`var`) as columns.

```{r create}
X <- matrix(as.numeric(1:12), nrow = 3)
obs <- data.frame(
  cell_type = c("T", "B", "T"),
  row.names = c("cell1", "cell2", "cell3")
)
var <- data.frame(
  highly_variable = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),
  row.names = c("gene1", "gene2", "gene3", "gene4")
)
adata <- AnnData(X, obs = obs, var = var)
adata
```

## Assign Slots

Annotations are aligned to `obs` or `var` and are kept in `obsm`, `varm`, `obsp`, `varp` and `layers`.
Unstructured data goes in `uns`.

```{r slots}
adata$obsm[["pca"]] <- matrix(c(0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 1, 2, 3), nrow = 3)
adata$layers[["counts"]] <- X * 2
adata$uns[["note"]] <- "example"
adata$obs[["batch"]] <- c("a", "a", "b")
adata
```

## Subset

Indexing is 1-based, and negative indices exclude.

```{r subset}
adata[1:2, ]
adata[-1, c("gene1", "gene3")]$shape
```

Subsetting returns a View, which shares data with the original `AnnData` and prints with a `View of ` prefix.
Modifying a View makes it an independent object and leaves the original unchanged, with a warning.

```{r view}
sub <- adata[1:2, ]
sub$is_view
sub$obs[["batch"]] <- c("x", "y")
sub$is_view
adata$obs[["batch"]]
```

Values extracted from a View are plain R objects, so unlike Python `x <- sub$X; x[1, 1] <- 0` does not change the View.
Assign through the View (`sub$X[1, 1] <- 0`) instead.

## Write and read h5ad

```{r h5ad}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5ad")
write_h5ad(adata, path)
roundtrip <- read_h5ad(path)
roundtrip
identical(roundtrip$obs_names, adata$obs_names)
```

Use `compression = "gzip"` to compress datasets, and `as_sparse` in `read_h5ad()` to read a dense `X` as a sparse matrix.

## Backed mode

`read_h5ad(backed = "r")` keeps `X` (and `raw$X`) on disk and reads only the parts that are indexed.
Everything else is read into memory.
Use `backed = "r+"` to write changes to `X` back to the file.

```{r backed}
backed <- read_h5ad(path, backed = "r")
backed$isbacked
backed$filename
backed$X[1:2, c(1, 3)]
```

`chunked_X()` visits the rows of `X` in chunks and `chunk_X()` returns random or chosen rows.

```{r chunks}
chunks <- backed$chunked_X(2)
length(chunks)
chunks[[2]]$start
backed$chunk_X(I(3))
```

`to_memory()` loads the whole object and `write_h5ad()` or `copy(filename)` write a backed object to a new file.
Assigning `X` ends backed mode, and the file is left unchanged.

```{r backed-memory}
in_memory <- backed$to_memory()
in_memory$isbacked
backed$file$close()
```

`sparse_dataset()` makes a handle on a sparse matrix in an open rhdf5 group, which also has `$append()` to add rows or columns on disk.

## Move a file to Python and back

The file written above can be read by Python anndata directly.
These chunks need Python so they are shown but not run.

```{python python-read, eval = FALSE, python.reticulate = FALSE}
import anndata as ad

adata = ad.read_h5ad("example.h5ad")
adata.obs["from_python"] = True
adata.write_h5ad("from-python.h5ad")
```

```{r read-back, eval = FALSE}
back <- read_h5ad("from-python.h5ad")
back$obs[["from_python"]]
```

## Write and read zarr

`write_zarr()` writes a zarr v3 store (a directory) and `read_zarr()` reads v3 and v2 stores.

```{r zarr}
zarr_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".zarr")
write_zarr(adata, zarr_path)
zarr_roundtrip <- read_zarr(zarr_path)
zarr_roundtrip
identical(zarr_roundtrip$obs_names, adata$obs_names)
```

Use the `compressors` argument to choose the compression (zstd, gzip, blosc or none) and `shards` to set the shard shape.
Writing zarr v2 is not yet supported.

## Move a zarr store to Python and back

Python anndata reads and writes the same store.
These chunks need Python so they are shown but not run.

```{python python-zarr, eval = FALSE, python.reticulate = FALSE}
import anndata as ad

adata = ad.read_zarr("example.zarr")
adata.obs["from_python"] = True
adata.write_zarr("from-python.zarr")
```

```{r zarr-read-back, eval = FALSE}
back <- read_zarr("from-python.zarr")
back$obs[["from_python"]]
```
